title: C3 glomerulonephritis
diseaseDescription: Bounded C3GN map: acquired convertase dysregulation, complement-regulatory and CFHR structural variants, glomerular complement deposition and variable renal course. Related mixed-C3G assay/cohort evidence and mixed-C3G/IC-MPGN trials retain separate contexts. Dense deposit disease and immune-complex GN are excluded as mapped phenotypes; their inclusion in cited studies is explicit. Selected proximal complement therapies include verified US indications through 2026-10-15; no universal causal circuit or comprehensive therapy catalog is claimed.
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of c3-glomerulonephritis-summary-candidate-3495bfd77080; external current-literature review remains pending. Overall scientific summary of c3-glomerulonephritis-appraised-candidate-c7fdac3e8a2c; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional automatic appraisal of c3-glomerulonephritis-candidate-002. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: C3 nephritic factors
entities.description: Autoantibodies with heterogeneous activity on the alternative-pathway C3 convertase.

entities.label: Alternative-pathway C3 convertase
entities.description: C3bBb enzyme complex; stabilization and susceptibility to regulation vary with nephritic factor and properdin.

entities.label: Alternative complement pathway dysregulation
entities.description: Selected acquired and genetic abnormalities identified in patients; not a universal single cause.

entities.label: Complement-regulatory gene variants
entities.description: Reported CFH, CFI, CD46 and CFHR variants in selected cohorts; pathogenicity is not assumed for every variant.

entities.label: Anti-factor H autoantibodies
entities.description: Heterogeneous antibodies studied in alternative-pathway glomerulopathies; their functional effects are sample-specific.

entities.label: Factor H regulatory activity
entities.description: Factor H cofactor activity and cell-surface protection are distinct assay endpoints.

entities.label: Glomerular complement deposits
entities.description: AP and terminal complement proteins detected by proteomics in C3GN glomeruli.

entities.label: C3GN renal phenotype
entities.description: Biopsy-defined C3GN with variable proliferative patterns, hematuria, proteinuria and clinical course; DDD is excluded.

entities.label: Iptacopan exposure
entities.description: Oral factor B inhibitor studied as an adjunct to background care in mixed C3 glomerulopathy; no subtype-specific estimate is inferred.

entities.label: Proteinuria
entities.description: Urinary protein excretion; trial UPCR is a surrogate endpoint, distinct from long-term kidney survival.

entities.label: CFHR5 exon 2–3 duplication
entities.description: Founder structural variant segregating with Cypriot CFHR5 nephropathy; not all CFHR5 variants or all C3GN.

entities.label: Duplicated-domain FHR5 protein
entities.description: Patient-serum FHR5 with duplicated N-terminal SCR1–2 domains; functional effects differ by assay.

entities.label: FHR5 surface-complement binding
entities.description: Recruitment of FHR5 to complement-coated erythrocyte membranes and mouse glomerular complement in the cited assay.

entities.label: Complement factor B
entities.description: Alternative-pathway C3-convertase component and direct molecular target of iptacopan.

entities.label: Complement C3 / C3b
entities.description: C3 and its activated fragment C3b; both are bound by pegcetacoplan.

entities.label: Loss of kidney function
entities.description: eGFR decline and current regulatory kidney-function endpoint; distinct from demonstrated prevention of kidney failure.

entities.label: Complement autoantibodies
entities.description: C3/C5/C4 nephritic factors and anti-factor antibodies studied in the modern C3G cohort; no universal driver is assumed.

entities.label: Pegcetacoplan exposure
entities.description: Randomized pegcetacoplan exposure in the mixed-diagnosis VALIANT trial; molecular therapy metadata is retained separately.

claims.text: Patient nephritic-factor IgG stabilized alternative-pathway C3 convertase in biochemical assays.
limitations: Mixed renal-disease population; assay activity does not establish C3GN causation or universal patient prevalence.

claims.text: C3 nephritic factors were the most common acquired alternative-pathway abnormality in the 12-case C3GN series.
limitations: Small selected case series; no population prevalence or causal sufficiency established.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: CFH, CFI and CFHR mutations were among the abnormalities reported in the C3GN series.
limitations: Individual variant function and penetrance cannot be resolved from the abstract.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Complement-regulatory gene mutations were detected in both proliferative and nonproliferative isolated-C3 glomerulonephritis groups, with differing frequencies.
limitations: Historical diagnostic categories predate modern C3G criteria; selected cohort and subgroup sizes limit generalization.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Glomerular proteomics identified alternative-pathway and terminal-complement proteins in the C3GN case series.
limitations: Deposited proteins do not by themselves prove the sequence or sufficiency of injury mechanisms.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Patients in the C3GN series typically had hematuria and proteinuria alongside glomerular complement deposits.
limitations: Clinicopathological association; does not prove deposits alone cause clinical manifestations.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Most patients with native kidney disease had stable renal function during reported follow-up, qualifying an inevitable progressive-failure interpretation.
limitations: Small selected series; this is not an estimate of long-term kidney survival for all C3GN.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Anti-factor H IgG from three glomerulopathy patients affected factor H factor-I cofactor activity in functional assays.
limitations: Broad glomerulopathy cohort; functional effect in three samples cannot be generalized to all C3GN or all anti-FH antibodies.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: In the reported assays, glomerulopathy anti-FH antibodies did not perturb factor H cell-surface protection or ligand binding.
limitations: Different regulatory functions are distinct endpoints; antibody detection alone does not establish universal functional inhibition.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: In APPEAR-C3G, iptacopan reduced 24-hour UPCR relative to placebo by 35.1% at six months on background care in adults with C3 glomerulopathy.
limitations: Mixed C3G enrollment; no C3GN-specific efficacy estimate or long-term kidney-survival benefit established by this abstract. Trial funded by Novartis.
Abstract-only source inspection; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: The familial CFHR5 exon 2–3 duplication encoded a circulating FHR5 protein with duplicated N-terminal SCR1–2 domains.
limitations: Founder variant; not all CFHR5 variation.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Mutant FHR5 bound less effectively than wild-type FHR5 to complement-coated erythrocyte membranes and glomerular-bound mouse complement in the reported binding assays.
limitations: Cross-system assay substrates; not a direct measurement of in-vivo human renal deposition.
The original assay supports reduced binding, not universal loss of FHR5 function.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: The reduced-binding result does not imply a simple loss of all FHR5 activity: mutant FHR5 had increased factor-I cofactor activity in the reported assay.
limitations: Qualifies extrapolation to generalized loss of function; the cofactor assay is a different endpoint from surface binding.
Supplementary raw assays not independently inspected.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: The CFHR5 founder duplication cosegregated with renal disease in Cypriot pedigrees with biopsy-confirmed C3GN; this allele was absent from the 36 sporadic UK/French C3GN cases tested.
limitations: Ascertainment, shared founder ancestry and incomplete mechanistic understanding limit generalization.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: A unique hybrid CFHR3-1 gene was associated with autosomal dominant complement-mediated glomerulonephritis in a reported family.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; no functional competition or convertase-stabilization mechanism is inferred for this hybrid.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: In the expanded CFHR5 founder cohort of 91 patients from 16 pedigrees, progression varied by sex and age; 18 developed end-stage renal disease.
limitations: Expansion of the Gale founder cohort, not independent replication; percentages are cohort-specific, not population prognosis.
Abstract-only inspection; historical CKD/ESRD terminology retained.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: In the modern C3G referral cohort, in-vitro convertase stabilization by autoantibodies correlated strongly with systemic complement biomarkers.
limitations: Retrospective referral cohort; biomarker/assay correlation does not establish prospective clinical causation.
Earlier Sethi and current Iowa referral datasets may overlap; independent replication is not assumed.

claims.text: Autoantibody mechanisms are not universal: more than half of the C3GN subgroup in the comprehensively characterized cohort had no identifiable driver; localized renal dysregulation was proposed, not demonstrated.
limitations: No detected driver is not proof of biological absence; nephritic factors change over time.
Major stated limitation: sparse longitudinal data; local glomerular dysregulation remains a hypothesis.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: Factor B and factor D were used with immobilized C3b to reconstitute alternative-pathway C3 convertase in the patient-IgG SPR experiments.
limitations: Biochemical reconstitution; not a C3GN clinical experiment.
Codex agent source check; independent domain review pending.

claims.text: C3NeF-stabilized convertase cleaved added C3 and deposited nascent C3b on the assay surface, with sample-dependent activity.
limitations: C3 and C3b are represented by a combined protein node; assay-surface deposition is not human glomerular deposition.

claims.text: In VALIANT (124 randomized patients with C3G or primary IC-MPGN), pegcetacoplan reduced UPCR relative to placebo by 68.1% at week 26 (95% CI 57.3–76.2).
limitations: Pooled mixed-diagnosis result; no C3GN-specific estimate or head-to-head comparison with iptacopan.
Apellis/Sobi funding; full methods/supplement not inspected.

claims.text: Proteinuria benefit did not establish every renal endpoint: the histologic activity score did not differ significantly in 69 evaluable biopsies, and subsequent endpoints including eGFR change were not formally tested in the original hierarchical analysis.
limitations: Historical trial-analysis qualification; distinguish from the later August 2026 FDA label that includes reduction of loss of kidney function.

limitations: US label mechanism statement, distinct from a new primary mechanistic experiment.

scientificSummary.scope: Bounded C3GN map: alternative complement pathway dysregulation, acquired convertase stabilization, complement-regulatory variants and glomerular complement deposition. Dense deposit disease is excluded as a phenotype; mixed C3 glomerulopathy studies are labelled and cannot establish C3GN-specific effects. Infection-related and immune-complex glomerulonephritis are excluded.

paragraphs.text: C3 glomerulonephritis comprises heterogeneous complement-associated kidney injury rather than a single universal circuit. C3GN biopsies and clinical series link alternative-pathway abnormalities with glomerular complement deposits, hematuria and proteinuria. Patient-IgG experiments show that nephritic factors can stabilize C3 convertase, but the classic assay cohort was predominantly dense deposit disease, and terminal-pathway activity varied between samples. Familial evidence identifies a different branch: a CFHR5 duplication cosegregated with C3GN and produced a protein with altered surface-complement binding; its increased cofactor activity argues against a simple loss of all function. CFHR3-1 rearrangements provide another familial association. These mechanisms remain incomplete: more than half of the C3GN subgroup in a modern comprehensively characterized cohort had no identifiable driver. Local glomerular dysregulation is a proposed explanation, not a demonstrated mechanism for that group.

Clinical course and treatment response also vary. Stable function in a small native-kidney C3GN series does not negate progression seen in the expanded CFHR5 founder cohort. In mixed-population randomized trials, iptacopan reduced proteinuria versus placebo by 35.1% at six months and pegcetacoplan by 68.1% at week 26; different populations and designs prevent a direct efficacy comparison or isolated C3GN estimate. The original VALIANT analysis did not show a significant histologic activity-score difference and did not formally test subsequent eGFR endpoints. Separately, the August 2026 US pegcetacoplan label includes reducing proteinuria and loss of kidney function in patients aged at least 12 with C3G or primary IC-MPGN; the inspected US iptacopan label covers proteinuria reduction in adults with C3G. Those regulatory statements do not establish lifelong prevention of kidney failure. Both labels warn of serious encapsulated-bacterial infections. This bounded, Consensus-assisted synthesis retains mixed-disease and assay limitations, incomplete screening and pending independent scientific review.
